html:
Company: Lithium-ion batteries producer · Home country: United Kingdom · Size: Large (250+ staff) · HS 850760 (Electrical & electronic equipment) · Generated 2026-11-21

1. Executive Summary

Verdict: ENTER WITH CAUTION. Real opportunity, but specific risks need a mitigation plan before scaling.

Market attractiveness: 7.2/10
Recommended entry mode: Wholly owned sales subsidiary (later local assembly if volumes justify)

  • Import market of €22.90 bn in 2024, growing 30.16% a year since 2019.
  • Supply is highly concentrated (HHI 7,374); top supplier China holds 85.69%.
  • CAGE distance from United Kingdom: low.
  • China supplies 85.69% of extra-EU imports.
  • Priority EU markets: Germany, Netherlands, Sweden.

HHI 7,374: Highly concentrated. A few suppliers dominate, so a newcomer must win share from incumbents or exploit buyers' wish to diversify supply (EU 'de-risking').

China's share of extra-EU imports moved from 46.47% (2019) to 85.69% (2024).

4. PESTEL Analysis

  • Political: Stable democracies with a single trade policy run by the European Commission. EU-China relations follow a 'de-risking' agenda: more trade-defence cases, the Foreign Subsidies Regulation and screening of Chinese investment.
  • Economic: Single market of ~450 million consumers and one of the world's largest import markets; high purchasing power, though growth is modest and varies strongly between member states. Latest: GDP growth 1.5% (2025), inflation 2.5% (World Bank).
  • Social: Diverse languages and consumer cultures across 27 countries; strong demand for sustainability, quality and data privacy; ageing population.
  • Technological: Advanced digital infrastructure and e-commerce; strict standards (CE, EN norms) make quality and certification a competitive factor. Fast innovation cycles; certification and cybersecurity rules tighten.
  • Environmental: European Green Deal: CBAM, Ecodesign/ESPR, Battery Regulation, deforestation and packaging rules raise compliance costs but reward low-carbon products.
  • Legal: Harmonised product law across the EU (one CE mark for 27 markets), GDPR for customer data, strong IP protection and contract enforcement.

5. CAGE Distance

Dimension Distance Evidence
Cultural Medium The EU spans 24 official languages; expect local-language marketing, labels and service in each priority country.
Administrative Medium Preferential access via EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement; rules of origin apply.
Geographic Low ~321 km between capitals.
Economic Low GDP per capita $57,602 (home) vs $47,089 (target), ratio 1.2x.

Overall distance: Low.

6. Tariffs, Trade Defence & Regulation

⚠️ Trade defence: Chinese firms dominate the battery value chain; China's export controls on graphite (2023) and battery technology affect supply chains.

  • CE marking: Low Voltage, EMC and Radio Equipment Directives
  • RoHS (hazardous substances) and WEEE (take-back and recycling, producer registration per member state)
  • EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 for products with batteries: carbon footprint, due diligence, battery passport phased in
  • General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (GPSR), applies to consumer products since Dec 2024
  • Union Customs Code: an EU-established importer/representative and EORI number are required
  • Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015: ban on products made with forced labour, applies from Dec 2027

Verify current duties and requirements: - Access2Markets (EU tariffs, rules of origin, requirements) - EU TARIC tariff database - EU trade defence cases

7. Risk Matrix

Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation
Dominant incumbent supplier (China, 85.69% share) High High Differentiate on quality, service, sustainability and EU/China-specific certification rather than price.
Trade-defence or retaliation measures in the EU-China corridor High High Monitor trade-defence notices; diversify sourcing and production locations; build tariff scenarios into pricing.
Brand and message mis-fit with local consumers Medium Medium Local consumer testing, native-language content, local marketplace and social channels.
Currency volatility (EUR/CNY/USD) Medium Medium Price in home currency where possible; hedge large contracts with forwards.

8. Recommended Entry Mode

Wholly owned sales subsidiary (later local assembly if volumes justify)

  • Attractive market and strong institutions justify full control for a large firm.
  • A subsidiary captures the full margin and builds direct customer relationships.
  • Within the EU one CE-compliant product and one importer of record give access to all 27 markets: start with 2-3 priority countries.
  • Inputs: attractiveness 7.2/10, CAGE distance low, institutional quality 6.8/10, company size large (250+ staff).

10. 90-Day Action Plan

  1. Days 1-30, validate: confirm the HS code and duty rate on official tariff tools, size the niche with customer interviews, shortlist 10 potential partners or channels in Germany, Netherlands, Sweden.
  2. Days 1-30, compliance: map required certifications and labelling (see section 6), get quotes from a test lab or regulatory agent, register trademarks in the target market.
  3. Days 31-60, commercial model: build a landed-cost and pricing model (duties, freight, VAT, channel margins, FX), and draft the partner or channel agreement.
  4. Days 31-60, go-to-market: localise product pages, packaging and sales material; pick 1-2 launch channels consistent with the entry mode: wholly owned sales subsidiary (later local assembly if volumes justify).
  5. Days 61-90, pilot: ship a pilot order or open the online store, track sell-through, margin and customer feedback against go/no-go KPIs.
